title: Sensor-agnostic own-signature/EM COP fusion as a TAK plugin, with disconnected tactical spectrum management (JRFL, assignments, interference tickets) and emitter-library distribution to cheap sensor fleets

scores.rationale: Own-signature exposure is a commander-level survival issue (Ukraine-style signature targeting) and DDIL EW planning has been an unmet requirement since Raven Claw in 2018 (FACT, HIGH: army.mil/199368, 2018; army.mil/291863, 2026-04-21); not a 5 because S2AS production (cpeisw.army.mil, 2026-06-01) and TLS-BCT (c4isrnet.com, 2024-12-12) now blunt the sharpest own-signature and threat-picture pain, leaving the cross-vendor fusion/offline-workflow seam.

Every command-post displacement, every exercise rotation and every EMI report exercises the seam; 25E spectrum managers run JRFL/assignment/JSIR workflows continuously per CJCSM 3320.01D and ATP 6-02.70 (FACT, MEDIUM), and TiC brigades now field S2AS, TLS-BCT and REWSI sensors simultaneously (FACT, HIGH: defensescoop.com 2026-09-11).

Only adjacent hardware/prime ceilings exist: S2AS $350M ceiling, REWSI $99M + $96.9M IDIQ ceilings, PrEPS $1.6B-$2.4B estimate (FACT, MEDIUM: executivegov.com PM EW&C forecast, 2026). No R-1/P-1 line, PE number or obligated dollar was found for sensor-agnostic fusion or a disconnected spectrum-management client; the card itself states 'Public evidence insufficient for the EWPMT-X FY26/FY27 line value'. Ceilings are not revenue.

PM EW&C demonstrably uses CSO/OTA vehicles open to non-traditionals (REWSI call 2026-04-24; ERIS CSO prototype awards to Pacific Defense Strategies, SRC and Herrick, executivegov.com/cpeisw.army.mil 2026-05-01, FACT, MEDIUM), but neither the REWSI call nor ERIS solicits a vendor-neutral fusion layer (ERIS is an electronic-attack/force-protection effort under PL EA, INFERENCE from search summaries). Two buyers (CPE ISW vs DISA DSO) with unconfirmed contracting offices (ACC-APG, DISA PSD both INFERENCE) and SBIR closed by the ownership test.

ATAK-CIV SDK, CoT and SigMF are open; five single-sensor TAK RF plugins prove the plumbing (FACT, MEDIUM: parsons.com/products/tems, github.com/jack-driscoll/atakrr). DDIL-tolerant time-aligned dedup across heterogeneous sensors with CRDT sync is moderate engineering, not research. Not a 5 because vendor export formats (S2AS, MOTH, Dragonfly, TLS) and JSDR/EMBM-J interfaces are undocumented publicly.

The card's own proof-of-concept estimate ($60k-$150k for two founders, KrakenSDR/USRP kits, one field demo) fits $250k, but the credible military demo ($0.8M-$2M: DFARS 7012 enclave, U.S.-person engineers, exercise access, vendor adapters) does not; $250k buys a demo, not a customer-grade proof (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

An ATAK-CIV plugin demo with two commercial SDR types and a simulated 30-minute outage is achievable in 3-6 months; a demo a PM EW&C product lead would credit (real S2AS/REWSI feeds, real SFAF data, an exercise slot) is 12-18 months away and gated by sponsor access rather than code (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

Own-signature and commercial-band recordings can be self-collected with COTS SDRs and SFAF-format synthetic data is buildable from public references, but everything that makes the product real - JSDR/JRFL records, unit emitter inventories, exercise own-signature data - is CUI requiring a government sponsor (FACT, MEDIUM: E07-F30), and threat emitter libraries are classified and inaccessible to an uncleared team (FACT, HIGH: E07-F21).

Score of 1 explained: the card rates burden 'high'. Software marketed for military EW/ES/direction-finding is likely reviewed under USML Category XI (ITAR), which has no deemed-export exception for the Indonesian co-founder (E07-F18, FACT, MEDIUM); all frequency plans, unit signatures and sensor positions are CUI from the first exercise (DFARS 252.204-7012 / NIST 800-171, CMMC clause effective 2025-11-10); FOCI review under 32 CFR 117.11 treats even a permanent resident as a foreign interest (E07-F19). Only an EAR99-scoped own-signature/interference-only product mitigates this, and that scoping requires export counsel - no legal judgment made here. Not 0 because a commercial spectrum-monitoring scope may plausibly fall under EAR.

The MVP (open schema, two commercial SDR adapters, DDIL sync, friendly-emitter heat map, offline JSIR-style queue) starts fully unclassified on ATAK-CIV, but the card rates classification dependence 'eventually': threat-emitter content, EWPMT-X classified integration and real JRFL data pull the product into CUI and then classified territory within the first customer engagement (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

Score of 1 explained: every slice already has a funded occupant. Own-signature: 3dB Labs S2AS production, 9 delivered by Aug 2026 (FACT, HIGH: cpeisw.army.mil 2026-06-01; defensescoop.com 2026-08-28). Joint spectrum management: Palantir-built EMBM-J DS (FACT, MEDIUM: militaryembedded.com 2025-04-21) plus a GEMSIS/EMBM-J SA recompete incumbent. EW planning host: EWPMT-X integrator (not public). Threat picture: CACI/Mastodon TLS-BCT. Data layer: Anduril Lattice in the NGC2 common data baseline (FACT, MEDIUM: army.mil/293409 2026-06). Sensor vendors Heaviside and RII each ship their own software. Plus five existing TAK RF plugins. Not 0 only because no one publicly owns the cross-vendor DDIL fusion seam today.

Score of 1 explained: incumbents are not vulnerable, they are freshly funded and contractually empowered. The REWSI call already requires MOSA/open APIs and NGC2 integration from sensor vendors (FACT, HIGH: defensescoop.com 2026-09-11), so the Army can obtain fusion-ready openness by mandate on existing vehicles; 3dB Labs can extend S2AS under its production contract; the EWPMT-X integrator can add fusion as a capability drop; none needs new technology (card incumbent_response, INFERENCE, HIGH). Not 0 because the EWPMT-X integrator and its scope remain unverified publicly.

The TAK plugin API is government-controlled and open (ATAK-CIV, FACT, HIGH), but the six systems that matter - S2AS, TLS-BCT, MOTH, Dragonfly, Spectrum XXI/JSDR/EMBM-J, NGC2/HYDRA - all have interfaces controlled by vendors or DISA DSO that are not public; TAK-GOV/MIL distribution rules add another gate (card integration_requirement, FACT/INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Feasible only with a sponsor who compels vendor cooperation.

Score of 1 explained: the card states 'code is not defensible' - multiple TAK RF plugins exist and ATAK-CIV is open. Every proprietary asset the company could build (vendor adapters, JSDR/EMBM-J interface agreements, TAK-GOV accreditation, exercise-derived datasets, 25E-validated workflow) is controllable by the government and transferable to an incumbent at will (INFERENCE, HIGH). Not 0 because a 25E-validated offline workflow and accumulated own-signature datasets would have some switching cost.

Civil analogues exist (public-safety event spectrum management, range/test-site monitoring, telecom interference hunting, critical-infrastructure RF awareness; TAK is used by DHS/CBP and public-safety agencies) but the card rates them 'few and price-sensitive', citing Aurora Insight's end in a Maxar acquisition rather than independent scale (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Dual use mainly reduces ITAR exposure rather than creating a market.

The core user base is a few thousand spectrum managers and CEMA staff (card, INFERENCE, MEDIUM); expansion into EW planning, threat ID or the NGC2 data layer runs directly into EWPMT-X, TLS-BCT and Lattice/Palantir lanes; allied expansion (NATO spectrum deconfliction, TAK variants) is plausible but 'Public evidence insufficient' per the card, and integrating for a foreign military raises ITAR defense-service exposure.

Software sustainment, adapter updates per new sensor and exercise support are recurring in principle, but with one or two 25E per brigade/division and government ownership of the TAK component (which the Army prefers), recurring revenue would be small sustainment task orders on a prime's vehicle rather than per-seat expansion (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

Score of 1 explained: (a) SBIR/STTR fails outright - the Indonesian founder's shares never count and the German founder's count only after the green card, so a 50/50 split fails 13 CFR 121.702 (FACT, HIGH: E07-F3); (b) likely ITAR Category XI subject matter makes sharing technical data with the Indonesian founder a deemed export needing DDTC authorization (E07-F18, FACT, MEDIUM); (c) three of the card's fatal-if-absent roles (tactical EW/SIGINT engineer, former 25E/spectrum manager, TAK plugin developer) are absent from a two-student team and must be recruited before anything credible exists; (d) both founders are years from clearance eligibility (E07-F21). Not 0 because the strong engineer can plausibly build the ATAK-CIV MVP and an EAR99-scoped civil version is founder-accessible.

market.summary: No distinct budget owner or software line - only adjacent hardware/prime ceilings (S2AS $350M, REWSI $196M, PrEPS $1.6B-$2.4B estimate); the two valuable slices already awarded to 3dB Labs and Palantir/DISA; the Army can obtain fusion-ready openness by mandating MOSA/APIs under REWSI rather than buying from a new vendor; a few-thousand-person user base split across two agencies; low technical barrier means value sits in access/accreditation, i.e., a subcontract niche; SBIR ownership test fails and ITAR/CUI exposure blocks the cheapest on-ramps. Accepted in full.

competition.summary: Own-signature (3dB Labs S2AS production, fielding underway) and joint spectrum management (Palantir-built EMBM-J DS, DISA recompete) are captured; the residual fusion layer sits inside EWPMT-X, which the Army fixed on TAK in 2024 so it or its integrator owns it; REWSI's MOSA/API mandate lets the Army compel sensor vendors to expose detections; Anduril Pulsar-L/Lattice is TAK-compatible and in the NGC2 baseline (Pulsar claims are RECALL/company marketing, MEDIUM). Accepted; this session's EWPMT-X search found no vendor-neutral fusion solicitation, and the one new PM EW&C CSO item found (ERIS, 2026-05-01) is an electronic-attack prototyping effort, not fusion software.

feasibility.summary: Timing/capture by incumbents; low technical barrier and therefore no code moat; required data (JSDR/JRFL/SFAF, vendor formats, exercise signatures) is CUI from day one and threat libraries are classified; founder fit is the sharpest blocker (SBIR fails on ownership, AFWERX limits foreign-national participation, ITAR has no deemed-export exception, FOCI treats a permanent resident as a foreign interest, clearances 5+ years out); market is a few thousand spectrum managers; credible military demo costs $0.8M-$2M versus $250k available. Accepted in full.

verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute with strength 4-5 and I find no evidence to overturn them; this session's two targeted searches confirmed that (a) no public solicitation, sources-sought or award exists for a vendor-neutral EWPMT-X fusion microservice (the only 2026 PM EW&C CSO item surfaced, ERIS, is an electronic-attack prototyping effort under PL EA - FACT, MEDIUM, executivegov.com / cpeisw.army.mil 2026-05-01), and (b) EWPMT-X remains an Army-USMC TAK-X pilot with a stated FY2026 replacement target and no public integrator contract (FACT, HIGH, army.mil/275843). The PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE chain is intact (CEMA/25E -> Cyber CoE -> PM EW&C / DISA DSO), but it breaks at CONTRACTING OFFICE (both INFERENCE, unconfirmed), BUDGET (no line for fusion software; only ceilings for adjacent hardware) and CONTRACT VEHICLE (no open competition for this scope; SBIR closed by 13 CFR 121.702), so the major penalty applies. Decisive reason: the two valuable slices were captured in 2025-2026 by funded incumbents (3dB Labs S2AS production, Palantir/DISA EMBM-J DS), and the residual sensor-agnostic fusion seam is one the Army can fill by contractual openness mandates on REWSI/S2AS vendors or by its EWPMT-X integrator without new technology - so even a flawless product has no buyer who needs to pay a new vendor. On top of that, the subject matter is likely USML Category XI, the data is CUI from the first exercise, the user base is a few thousand people, and the founder structure fails SBIR while creating deemed-export exposure for the Indonesian co-founder. Market attractiveness 2.3/5 and founder fit 2.2/5 are analytical heuristics, not facts. Confidence HIGH that this is not a venture-scale, founder-accessible company; MEDIUM on the exact EWPMT-X ownership facts, which are not public.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not recommended as a company, but if the founders insist on this domain the only survivable slice is the skeptics' EAR99-scoped offline workflow client: a disconnected JRFL/SFAF-assignment/JSIR-interference-ticket tool for 25E spectrum managers (and civil public-safety/range spectrum coordinators) that queues offline and syncs on reconnect, deliberately excluding threat-emitter content, direction-finding and EW/ES features, delivered as an open ATAK-CIV plugin and sold as a subcontracted feature to a REWSI/S2AS prime or under a CRADA - a small services/IP-licensing business, not a venture-scale outcome, and still requiring export counsel to confirm EAR jurisdiction before design starts.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders with $250,000 pursued G11 anyway, the rational first build is not the full EM COP: it is an open ATAK-CIV plugin plus TAK Server microservice implementing a published detection schema (SigMF metadata plus Cursor-on-Target extensions), adapters for two commercial sensors (KrakenSDR for bearing, RTL-SDR/USRP for occupancy), CRDT-style DDIL sync, a friendly-emitter heat map scored against an imported SFAF assignment list, and an offline JSIR-style interference-ticket queue - roughly $60k-$150k and 3-6 months. They would show it to a National Guard or ROTC unit at a field exercise, then to TiC division CEMA chiefs, a Cyber CoE spectrum capability developer and, through them, the PM EW&C product leads for EWPMT-X and S2AS, and to 3dB Labs, Heaviside or RII as a subcontract pitch. The demonstration would prove that heterogeneous detections converge into one picture with an acceptable false-track rate, that the picture survives and reconverges after a simulated 30-minute outage, and that a 25E can produce a JRFL/EMI ticket offline faster than with spreadsheets. The customer would care because own-signature exposure is now a commander-level survival issue and DDIL EW planning has been unmet since Raven Claw in 2018. But this is exactly where the case fails: an incumbent can trivially crush them because 3dB Labs already holds the funded own-signature production contract with fielding underway, the Army can compel Heaviside, RII and 3dB Labs to expose detections through REWSI's existing MOSA/API terms, the EWPMT-X integrator can absorb fusion as a capability drop, and Anduril Lattice already sits in the NGC2 data baseline - none of them needs new technology, and the government controls every asset (exercise access, accreditation, vendor adapters, CUI data) that would otherwise become the startup's moat. The only milestone that would justify the next $2-5 million would be a signed OTA/CSO award or a prime subcontract under which PM EW&C explicitly designates a third-party, government-owned fusion microservice as the EWPMT-X common EM picture, with real S2AS/REWSI feeds and JSDR data flowing to the company inside a DFARS 7012 enclave and with export counsel having cleared an EAR-scoped product structure for the founding team; absent that, the next $2-5 million funds a subcontracting shop, and the honest recommendation is to redirect the $250,000 to a gap where the founders can own the seam.
bear_case_summary: The two valuable slices (own-signature via 3dB Labs S2AS production, joint spectrum management via Palantir-built EMBM-J DS) were awarded in 2025-2026 to funded incumbents; the residual sensor-agnostic fusion seam sits inside EWPMT-X scope that the Army can assign to its integrator or obtain by mandating MOSA/APIs from REWSI sensor vendors without new technology; no budget line, solicitation or award exists for third-party fusion software (this session's searches found only the ERIS electronic-attack CSO); the user base is a few thousand people; code is not defensible and every moat asset is government-controlled; the subject matter is likely ITAR Category XI with CUI data from day one; and the founder structure fails SBIR ownership while creating deemed-export and FOCI exposure. Three independent skeptics (strengths 5, 4, 5) and the evidence card's own killer_risk reach the same conclusion.
bull_case_summary: The pain is real and doctrinally documented: DDIL EW planning has been unmet since 2018, heterogeneous cheap sensors (S2AS, MOTH, Dragonfly, TLS-BCT) are multiplying faster than any common picture, spectrum managers still triage JRFL and EMI reports in spreadsheets when disconnected, and Lightning Surge showed EW data must feed the NGC2 common data layer. The Army fixed TAK as the government-owned EWPMT-X host, opening a plugin path; ATAK-CIV, CoT and SigMF are open; PM EW&C demonstrably uses CSO/OTA vehicles that carry no citizenship test; no vendor has a public incentive to build vendor-neutral fusion; and a narrow EAR99-scoped offline spectrum-management workflow could be founder-accessible and dual-use. The bull case is a credible small business, not a venture-scale company.
